macro_blurb: Escalating US-Iran tensions dominate risk sentiment today after Washington launched fresh strikes on Iran, with Trump reinstating a port blockade and floating a 20% toll on cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz, sending both stocks and bonds lower on energy and shipping-route concerns. Monetary policy adds a second layer: Fed Governor Waller floated the possibility of a near-term rate hike, a hawkish signal that pressures US duration and rate-sensitive EU equity sectors. In Asia-linked exposure, the FT reports investors are trimming positions in Asian chipmakers, a theme that spills into European and US semiconductor names. For Berlin-based traders, the mix of Middle East supply-route risk, a hawkish Fed tilt, and cooling semiconductor enthusiasm defines today's cross-asset backdrop.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a yield-and-value book, not a growth book. Nine of ten names carry a Yield percentile — average 90.1 — and average Value sits at 85.1, while Quality lags at 64.8. Six of ten picks are European, and the sector spread is deliberately defensive-income: 2 Utilities, 2 Consumer Defensive, plus Real Estate, Communication Services and Financial Services filling out the middle. Dividend yields run from Edenred's 5.64% to Landsec's 13.31%, and five names trade below 15x trailing earnings. This is a screen buying cash flow and payouts, not compounders — average Quality of 64.8 with three names showing negative ROE (Covestro -9.4%, KHC -12.6%) tells you the model is tolerating operational strain to get to the multiple.

The clearest thread is the EU income-utility complex: RED.MC (5.2% yield, 16.4x), LAND.L (13.31% yield, 0.76x book) and MONY.L (6.45% yield, 34% ROE) all surface on Yield + Value as UK/Iberian rate-sensitive payers — but Waller's hawkish rate-hike float cuts directly against that duration trade, so read these picks against a Fed that may not cooperate. A second thread runs through US deep-value income: HPQ (9.2x, 4.97% yield) and KHC (0.71x book, 6.44% yield) are both cheap-with-a-reason, KHC explicitly so with negative ROE.

The outlier is 1COV.DE at composite 100 — a loss-making chemical name riding an ADNOC bid, pure event risk, not factor exposure. The conspicuous absence is Healthcare, Industrials, Basic Materials and Energy — zero picks across four sectors out of 830 scored names, with Energy's absence particularly loud given Trump's Hormuz toll and fresh Iran strikes. Watch two things over the next fortnight: any Fed follow-through on Waller's hike signal (hits RED, ES, LAND directly), and Hormuz escalation, which would reprice the entire defensive-yield book against a supply-shock inflation impulse.
